root_cause.text: Off-by-one bounds check errors in the rockchip rkcif MIPI capture driver, where comparisons used `>` instead of `>=`, allowing array access one element beyond the end when the index equals the array size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE` to `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)` and similar for `index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX` and `id > RKCIF_ID_MAX`, correcting the off-by-one oversight that permitted out-of-bounds access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace static bounds checks with dynamic array-size checks to correctly support multiple hardware variants in the Rockchip MIPI interface driver.
intent_record.what: In the rkcif_mipi_get_reg function, the bounds checks for 'block' and 'index' were changed from comparing against constants RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE and RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX to comparing against ARRAY_SIZE of the corresponding arrays in rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks and rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs, and the comparison operators were changed from > to >=.
intent_record.how: This change makes the bounds checking dynamic, using the actual array sizes from the hardware-specific match data. It ensures that the warning and early return are triggered only when the index is actually out of bounds for the given hardware variant, preventing false positives or missed detections.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bound checks to use dynamic array sizes instead of hardcoded constants to prevent out-of-bounds access and support varying hardware configurations.
intent_record.what: Replaced three static constant-based upper bound checks (block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE, id > RKCIF_ID_MAX, index > RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX) with dynamic array size checks using ARRAY_SIZE on mipi->blocks, mipi->regs_id, and mipi->regs_id[id], and changed the operators from > to >=.
intent_record.how: The validation of block, id, and index now uses the actual dimensions of the arrays in match_data instead of fixed constants. This prevents out-of-bounds access when the arrays are smaller than the old constants, and allows correct access when the arrays are larger.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces bounds checks using `>` instead of `>=` for array indices. In `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg`, the check `WARN_ON_ONCE(id > RKCIF_ID_MAX)` uses `>`, but the loop `for (unsigned int j = 0; j < RKCIF_ID_MAX; j++)` in `rkcif_mipi_register` suggests `RKCIF_ID_MAX` is the array size (e.g., 4). Thus, `id > RKCIF_ID_MAX` permits the index to equal the array size, causing an out-of-bounds access. Similarly, `block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE` and `index > ...` checks may also be off-by-one based on constant definitions. The fix would require changing `>` to `>=` in all these comparisons. This is the initial commit of the driver, so the fix is not present.
